summary: This is a careful, well‑executed preregistered paired study that evaluates a verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks in a Mininet emulation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The experimental execution and archived artifacts appear consistent with the preregistration; the confirmatory analysis (exact McNemar two‑sided) was run as declared and did not reject (p = 0.125). The manuscript correctly treats the bootstrap CI as exploratory. Key reproducibility artifacts (preregistration, master prompt locator and SHA‑256, model configuration, raw responses, deterministic verifier traces, analysis code, and hash manifests) are present in the evidence bundle. Overall the study is scientifically useful and modestly novel (applies a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory design to multi‑vendor template emulation), but several presentation and provenance clarifications are required before finalisation.
critical_issues: References presented in the manuscript must appear as a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/identifier when appropriate). The review excerpts show numeric in‑text citations, but the submission must include a complete IEEE‑format References section; verify each cited record actually supports the nearby claim (do not leave any cited entry as a bare DOI/identifier or arXiv/identifier only).

The Disclosure Statement currently duplicates execution accounting and many internal artifact paths. Per the track guidance, condense the Disclosure Statement to a concise provenance and process summary while preserving exactly one immutable master_prompt locator and its full SHA‑256 digest. Remove run‑internal path lists and full per‑file hashes from the prose (these may remain in the archived evidence bundle).

Ambiguity in provider_call/stage/condition accounting wording: the execution manifest shows 200 shared_initial_generation events and 4 repair calls; some manifest fields label counts as {"shared":200, "guarded":4}. The manuscript must clarify explicitly (in Methods and Disclosure) that shared_initial_candidate semantics were used (one sampled initial generation per intent reused by baseline and guarded), that baseline is the immediate scoring of that shared initial candidate, and that the guarded pipeline only invoked up to one repair call for 4 intents (i.e., the observed paired differences derive only from verifier/repair actions and not from independent re‑generation). Avoid any phrasing implying baseline and guarded had independent initial model generations.

The manuscript reports an exploratory paired bootstrap percentile CI despite sparse discordant pairs (n10+n01 small). While labeling the CI exploratory is appropriate, add an explicit short caution in Methods/Results about the limitations of bootstrap CIs in small‑discordance paired binary data and avoid implying the CI is confirmatory; if citing a statistical reference to support this caution, include it in the IEEE References list.

The Disclosure Statement must include the mandatory immutable initial_master_prompt locator and SHA‑256 exactly once (this is present in the evidence bundle) and must not expand into an audit log; ensure the master_prompt line is preserved verbatim and placed succinctly within the condensed Disclosure Statement.
required_revisions: Include a conventional IEEE numbered References section containing full bibliographic metadata for every cited record. For each in‑text citation, ensure the cited source supports the specific claim. Replace any bare DOI/arXiv/identifier entries in the manuscript References with full citation entries (author(s), title, venue, year, DOI/URL as appropriate).

Condense the Disclosure Statement in the manuscript so it is concise and non‑duplicative of archived logs. It must (a) name the declared model(s) and provider(s), (b) identify the adapter/validator/task‑generator identifiers, (c) state the preregistration identifier and that it preceded model calls, (d) give exactly one immutable initial_master_prompt locator path and its full SHA‑256 digest, and (e) briefly state the human Research Director role and the post‑lock autonomous activities. Remove per‑file internal paths, per‑file hashes, and long execution manifest excerpts from the prose (they may remain in the archived artifact bundle).

Add an explicit, unambiguous statement in Methods (and repeat in the Disclosure Statement) that the study used shared_initial_candidate sampling semantics as preregistered: exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded episodes; baseline success is the validator score on that initial candidate, guarded success results from applying the deterministic validator and permitting up to one verifier‑triggered repair. Clearly state that any between‑condition differences within a pair therefore arose only from validator/repair actions, not from different first‑pass model samples.

Clarify provider_call/stage accounting language in Methods/Results so readers can unambiguously reconcile reported model_call counts: explicitly report the audited hosted_model_call_event_count (204), its decomposition (200 initial shared generations + 4 repair calls), and how stage_counts and condition_counts relate to the shared_initial_candidate design (explain fields labeling 'shared' vs 'guarded' in the manifest).

In Results or Methods add a concise caution about the bootstrap CI reliability in sparse‑discordant paired binary data (n10+n01 small), noting that bootstrap percentile intervals can be unstable in this regime and reiterate that the preregistered exact McNemar test is the formal confirmatory test (p = 0.125). If possible, include a brief supporting citation in the References (formatted in IEEE style).
optional_revisions: Consider adding a short table or appendix (kept within the 5‑page limit) that lists per‑vendor/template stratum counts and the per‑stratum discordant counts to help readers gauge heterogeneity (this can be brief and drawn from archived artifacts).

Optionally provide an exact conditional confidence interval or an exact mid‑p interval for the paired risk difference (labeled exploratory) alongside the bootstrap percentile CI to help triangulate effect size in the sparse discordant setting (do not require rerunning experiments; use existing archived paired contingency table to compute and report if already available).

Add one or two short citations in Methods to authoritative discussions of McNemar exact testing and of bootstrap behavior with small discordant counts to support the statistical cautions (ensure full IEEE citation entries).
